subject: Scheduling: Performance/Latency benchmarking review for EdgeScale POC
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@edgescale.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@edgescale.ai>
Date: 2026-08-29T15:03:00Z
Subject: EdgeScale POC - perf/latency benchmark review & scheduling

Michael — thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team wants to run through a focused benchmarking review to align on token throughput targets, SLOs, and the exact load plan for the POC (we want to avoid surprises before procurement signs off).

High-level asks:
- Walkthrough of expected median p50/p95 latency at the 25k tps target
- Confirmation of batching + KV cache behavior for our streaming workload
- Test plan: steady-state and spike scenarios, plus a short soak run

Attached is the initial load plan (edgescale-mtp-loadplan.xlsx). Can we schedule a 60–75 minute architecture + perf readout next week? Proposed windows (PT):
- Tue 2026-08-31 09:00–10:30
- Wed 2026-09-01 11:00–12:30

We’re flexible on attendees — I’ve copied Leah (eng lead) and procurement for timeline alignment.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Engineering
EdgeScale Systems

Attachment: edgescale-mtp-loadplan.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@edgescale.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-29T18:20:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeScale POC - perf/latency benchmark review & scheduling

Samir — thanks for the plan, I skimmed the spreadsheet. We should definitely do 75 min to leave room for the soak readout and Q&A. Internal attendees I suggest: Laura (APAC infra/ops), Karthik (serving runtime owner) and Dylan (perf lead) — I CC'd Laura.

Quick requests before we lock a slot:
- Can you add the concrete token-per-request distribution (p50/p95 request lengths) so we can size the KV cache behavior?
- Can you confirm whether you want dedicated capacity reserved for the run or if hosted API with reserved burst is acceptable? That affects how we prepare the kernels/quantization profile.

Of your two windows, the Tue 09:00 PT works best for our US engineers; Laura prefers Wed mornings APAC are possible but it pushes us late on the east coast. Propose we book Tue 2026-08-31 09:00–10:15 PT as tentative and I’ll coordinate with Laura for a timezone-friendly fallback.

I’ll attach our benchmark checklist (redwood-benchmark-checklist.pdf) and outline an agenda if we confirm.

— Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T02:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeScale POC - perf/latency benchmark review & scheduling

Thanks — looping in a constraint from infra: we have a planned capacity maintenance window that morning (APAC region) that could affect the Tue 09:00 PT slot if we need to test across regions. If the test is strictly US-west hosted, Tue is fine; if EdgeScale wants multi-region coverage we should move to Wed 2026-09-01 to avoid the maintenance overlap.

Karthik — please be prepared to speak to kernel selection/quantization strategy if we end up using a smaller model variant during the spike tests. Also, Dylan will need a full hour of control-plane access to toggle routing fallbacks for the soak.

Laura Bennett
Head of Production Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@edgescale.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@edgescale.ai>, procurement@edgescale.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeScale POC - perf/latency benchmark review & scheduling

Laura — good catch on the maintenance window. We only need US-west for the initial pass, so Tue 08/31 09:00 PT works for us. We’ll aim to test single-region first and then expand later if the results are good.

I attached a slimmed load plan with token-distribution per request and a short notes tab (edgescale-mtp-loadplan_v2.xlsx). Procurement looped in for timing and contract questions.

Samir

Attachment: edgescale-mtp-loadplan_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgescale.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T12:05:00Z
Subject: Confirmed: Tue 2026-08-31 09:00 PT — EdgeScale perf/latency readout (agenda + prep)

All — confirmed for Tue 2026-08-31 09:00–10:15 PT (60–75 mins). Calendar invite sent: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234

Proposed agenda (45–60 min readout, 15 min Q&A / contract items):
1) 5 min — introductions and objectives (Samir/Leah)
2) 15 min — EdgeScale workload profile & test targets (Samir)
3) 20 min — Redwood architecture walk & kernel/quantization choices for target throughput (Karthik + Laura)
4) 15 min — Live readout plan: soak + spike methodology, metrics captured, and runbook (Dylan)
5) 10–15 min — Q&A, procurement next steps (Samir + procurement)

Pre-reads: redwood-benchmark-checklist.pdf (attached), edgescale-mtp-loadplan_v2.xlsx (Samir). Please add any items you want covered. Dylan — can you take the runbook owner for the soak/spike and add a 10-minute dry run at 08:40 PT to validate permissions and metrics capture?

Thanks — I’ll attach the checklist to the invite and request a shared Drive folder for logs.

— Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xyz
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@edgescale.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T18:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Confirmed: Tue 2026-08-31 09:00 PT — EdgeScale perf/latency readout (agenda + prep)

Got it — I’ll own the runbook and bring per-step perf graphs for the spike scenarios. I’ll create a short checklist for instrumentation that the EdgeScale team should verify (prometheus endpoints, trace sampling, and token-length histograms).

Also confirming the 08:40 PT dry run — please make sure the engineer doing the run has control-plane creds for toggling the model variant; if not, we’ll need a 5-min buffer at 08:35 to provision.

Dylan Brooks
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
